_summary: Of 172 emitted grids, an estimated ~50 (range 45-60) are REAL distinct salary schedules; the other ~120 (~70%) are over-extraction. Drivers: (a) the full salary appendix is printed 3x — once per contract year (2014-15 ~pp326-350, 2015-16 ~pp360-390, 2016-17 ~pp395-410), so the same ~20 schedule types recur per year (real when values change annually, but many small flat differentials — coordinating 424/848, bilingual, activity 973-2811, one-time stipends 270/540 — are reprinted IDENTICALLY across all 3 years); (b) 56 of 172 files carry a __pNNN page suffix that duplicates a matching base file (page-pinned re-extractions); (c) multi-page big tables (D/T/L 'Special Services','Preparation Salary','(Continued)') fragment into several grids that belong to ONE schedule; (d) label-variant twins of the same table (differential_activity vs differentials_activity_rates, one_time_stipends vs table_5_one_time_stipends, pay_scale_group vs appendix_e, 5_differentials_coordinating vs differentials_coordinating, degree_differentials vs (L)_salary_table degree-diffs, additional/other/table_4 bilingual variants). Collapsing page-suffix + normalized-name groups already reduces 172 -> 114 (year,name) groups; folding continuation-fragments, variant-twins, and cross-year-identical small differentials brings real distinct schedules to ~50. In the 30-grid sample, 3 exact intra-sample duplicate pairs/sets were seen (coordinating ECC x2 same year; plus cross-year reprints).
